statement: In a graph $G = (V, E, \Phi)$, a finite walk is a sequence of edges $(e_1, e_2, \dots, e_{n-1})$ for which there is a sequence of vertices $(v_1, v_2, \dots, v_n)$ such that $\Phi(e_i) = \{v_i, v_{i+1}\}$ for $i = 1, 2, \dots, n-1$. A trail is a walk in which all edges are distinct. A path is a trail in which all vertices $v_1, v_2, \dots, v_n$ (and therefore also all edges) are distinct. For a directed graph $G = (V, E, \Phi)$, a directed path is a finite or infinite sequence of edges directed in the same direction joining a sequence of distinct vertices, such that $\Phi(e_i) = (v_i, v_{i+1})$ for $i = 1, 2, \dots, n-1$ and all vertices are distinct.

symbols.meaning: number of vertices in the finite path

properties.property: In a path, all edges are distinct.
properties.why: vertices are distinct, which implies distinct endpoint pairs for consecutive edges

properties.property: If there is a finite walk between two distinct vertices, then there is also a finite trail and a finite path between them.
properties.why: intermediate cycles in the walk can be bypassed to form a sequence of distinct vertices

properties.property: Two internally disjoint paths are edge-disjoint, but the converse is not necessarily true.
properties.why: sharing no internal vertices precludes sharing any connecting edges, while edge-disjoint paths may still meet at vertices

properties.property: The weight of a path in a weighted graph is the sum of the weights of the traversed edges.
properties.why: defined as the additive accumulation of weights over all edges in the path

properties.property: The distance between two vertices is the length of a shortest path between them, or infinity if no path exists.
properties.why: defined as the minimal length among paths connecting the pair

assumptions.assumption: All vertices in the vertex sequence of the path are distinct.
assumptions.breaks_when: A vertex is repeated (v_i = v_j for some i != j), turning the sequence into a non-path walk or trail.

assumptions.assumption: In a directed path, every edge is oriented in the direction of traversal such that \Phi(e_i) = (v_i, v_{i+1}).
assumptions.breaks_when: An edge is traversed against its specified orientation or lacks orientation.

failure_modes.cause: No sequence of edges exists connecting the two vertices in the graph.

failure_modes.signature: Sequence qualifies as a walk or trail, but fails the path definition
failure_modes.cause: The sequence visits an already traversed vertex.

failure_modes.mode: Opposing edge traversal in directed graph
failure_modes.signature: Edge sequence cannot form a directed walk or directed path
failure_modes.cause: An edge along the sequence has incidence (v_{i+1}, v_i) instead of (v_i, v_{i+1}).
